The code snippet confirms this by operating on `rendered_image` (which has dimensions H, W, 3) using matrix multiplication and addition. Since the operation is performed on the final 2D image tensor (H, W, 3) and does not involve depth or volume data, it is independent of volume resolution.

*   Input: A rendered RGB image tensor $I_{in}$ of shape $(3, H, W)$, and an image identifier (filename/name) [S1, unofficial].

The claim describes a specific image processing pipeline: taking an RGB tensor, retrieving exposure data (matrix and bias) by image name, permuting dimensions, applying the linear transform and bias, and returning the result. The provided source text [S1] explicitly contains the code snippet `torch.matmul(rendered_image.permute(1, 2, 0), exposure[:3, :3]).permute(2, 0, 1) + exposure[:3, 3, None, None]` and the line `exposure = pc.get_exposure_from_name(viewpoint_camera.image_name)`. This code directly implements the operations described in the claim (permutation, matrix multiplication with the 3x3 part of the exposure tensor, addition of the 3D bias part, and retrieval by image name). Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
